transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC — Duration 58m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Laura (CTO, Summit), Victor (Head of Platform), Anita (Security Lead), Marcus (SRE)
Summary: initial POC scoping focused on security/compliance for pilot, workload sizing for benchmarks, and clear success criteria and timeline. Customer emphasized SOC 2 and ISO requirements, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging, and on-prem/VPC constraints for sensitive workflows.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): hey everyone thanks for joining, can we do quick intros and the goal for today is to align on what a 2-4 week pilot looks like, what security artifacts you need, and what benchmark we'll run
00:27 Speaker 2 (Laura): yeah thanks Jordan. we want to validate that we can serve sensitive documents inside our VPC for the pilot, and that audit logs and key management meet our compliance team standards. timeline ideally two weeks for smoke, then a three week deeper run
00:52 Speaker 3 (Riley): quick clarifying q — when you say VPC, you mean private deployment (redwood private) or hosted with VPC peering? there are a couple of options with different security tradeoffs
01:12 Speaker 2 (Laura): right so prefer a private deployment for the most sensitive set, but we could start with hosted if the logs and encryption are proven. our blocker is SOC 2 evidence and SAML SSO into our IdP
01:35 Speaker 4 (Anita): and ISO 27001 certification status, plus RBAC that can map to our teams. also we need immutable audit logs for at least 12 months, plus exports to our SIEM
01:52 Speaker 3 (Riley): got it. Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SSO flows, RBAC groups, and can stream audit events to a syslog or S3 bucket. we'll include details in the security pack but to be clear, for pilot we can enable audit log streaming and KMS integrations
02:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): for acceptance criteria let's propose: throughput target of 150 concurrent requests with p95 latency under 800ms on our sample data, and no data leakage to other tenants, SOC2 artifacts supplied, and SSO working end-to-end
02:40 Speaker 5 (Victor): can you quantify tokens per second? our prompts average 600 tokens including context, and we expect bursts of 20 rps sustained for short periods
03:05 Speaker 3 (Riley): ok that matters for batching and memory. initial benchmark plan: 1) single model hosted on dedicated A100 pool, 2) seq length 1024/2048 profiles, 3) concurrency matrix 1/10/50/150, 4) measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput tokens/sec, and 5) measure GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates
03:38 Speaker 4 (Anita): encryption at rest — we require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and proof that logs of key access are available. is that supported in private mode?
03:55 Speaker 3 (Riley): yes, private deployments can use customer KMS; for hosted we offer envelope encryption but we can configure a dedicated HSM for enterprise (requires enterprise contract). will document options
04:20 Speaker 2 (Laura): data residency: EU only for this pilot. can the pilot nodes be pinned to a EU region?
04:32 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yes we can route to EU regions and pin capacity. for private on-prem it's trivial — we can deploy into your VPC or on-prem cluster. for hosted, we'll provision EU-only capacity and show network paths
05:00 Speaker 6 (Marcus): what about audit logs schema — fields we'll need: user id, route, model version, token counts, request/response hashes, timestamps, and correlation id for tracing
05:22 Speaker 3 (Riley): that's exactly what we can provide. logs are JSON lines with those fields, can stream to S3 or push to your SIEM via forwarder. retention is configurable, default 90 days, we can extend to 12 months for the pilot
05:50 Speaker 2 (Laura): good. on RBAC we need role separation: devs, platform, security, and restricted export role. can roles be mapped to SAML groups?
06:05 Speaker 3 (Riley): yes SAML/SCIM integration maps groups to RBAC roles. we'll share SCIM mapping examples in the security pack
06:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): shifting to benchmarks — what's your definition of success beyond latency? also quality/regression thresholds?
06:40 Speaker 2 (Laura): success = parity with our baseline in intent extraction and reranking tasks. we'll provide a small evaluation set and require < 3% regression in our intent F1 and top-1 rerank accuracy compared to current model. plus throughput and latency targets met
07:05 Speaker 3 (Riley): good. we'll run qualitative evals and attach the eval results to canary rollouts so you can flag regressions. for bench hardware we'll test A100 and H100 quantized variants to show cost/latency tradeoffs
07:30 Speaker 5 (Victor): any constraints on sequence length when using quantized kernels? we saw odd slowdowns at 4k seq on other runtimes
07:45 Speaker 3 (Riley): yes, kernel selection matters. we'll include profile results for 512/1024/2048/4096 seq. quantization helps cost but may affect latency at very long sequences; we'll show tradeoffs
08:02 Speaker 4 (Anita): compliance question — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs we can review? we need auditor contact or report redacted copy
08:20 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate; we'll send redacted reports and a SOC 2 summary that maps controls to your requirements. also include penetration test summaries
08:40 Speaker 2 (Laura): also require vulnerability disclosure policy and process for incident response and timelines for notifications (we need 72 hours SLA)
08:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): standard IR process is 72 hours notification for critical incidents; we'll include escalation contacts in the pack
09:10 Speaker 6 (Marcus): network considerations — do you require VPN, private link, or is VPC peering enough? our security team prefers private link with strict egress rules
09:30 Speaker 3 (Riley): we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and on-prem installations. for the pilot we can do PrivateLink into your VPC and lock down outbound egress. we'll provide network ACLs and ports list
09:55 Speaker 2 (Laura): great. on data retention and deletion — if we run the pilot on private deployment, can we guarantee data is purged at end of pilot and provide proof?
10:12 Speaker 3 (Riley): yes we'll provide deletion receipts and can run cryptographic wipe or reclaim nodes; for hosted we provide data deletion APIs and retention configs and can generate audit evidence
n10:35 Speaker 4 (Anita): how about logs that might contain PII — do you mask or provide redaction hooks?
10:50 Speaker 3 (Riley): we can integrate pre-processing hooks to mask sensitive fields, and we offer token redaction and PII detectors as part of the pipeline
n11:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): timelines — propose: security docs by 7/10, initial smoke bench in EU region week of 7/20 (48 hours), deeper benchmark and quality eval 7/27–8/7, and final go/no-go review 8/10. is that feasible?
11:30 Speaker 2 (Laura): that aligns with our target. procurement wants evidence before procurement sign-off though so the security pack is high priority
11:50 Speaker 3 (Riley): ok for the benchmark specifics we'll need: sample dataset (we can accept anonymized subset), traffic profile CSV, target model (you'll pick from our catalog), and acceptance thresholds. we'll draft a benchmark plan and share by 7/14
12:20 Speaker 5 (Victor): acceptance thresholds: p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.5s, throughput >= 150 rps sustained for 5 min, and accuracy regression < 3% on provided eval set
12:45 Speaker 4 (Anita): also require audit log integrity checks (signed logs) and retention 12 months for the pilot with daily export to our SIEM
13:05 Speaker 3 (Riley): signed logs are supported via HMAC and can be forwarded to your S3 with lifecycle policies; we'll include proof-of-concept in the benchmark run
13:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): ok let's capture action items and owners — Maya will compile the security pack, Riley the benchmark plan, Jordan will coordinate timeline and cost, and Summit to provide data/traffic.
13:55 Speaker 2 (Laura): yep we'll circulate internal stakeholders and get you the sample dataset and traffic by 7/12
14:10 Speaker 6 (Marcus): one more question — are there costs for running dedicated A100/H100 test rigs? we need estimate for both hosted dedicated and private on-prem run costs
14:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we'll share a cost worksheet with run-hours, avg token cost, and dedicated reservation pricing. initial estimate by 7/12. for on-prem we'll provide a BOM and sizing guidance
14:52 Speaker 5 (Victor): do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback if a variant exceeds latency thresholds? we want safe degradation
15:10 Speaker 3 (Riley): yes, rollout policies can be configured to canary at 10% with auto-fallback to a smaller model or cached responses if latency crosses threshold. we'll demo that in the bench run
15:35 Speaker 4 (Anita): last compliance ask — SSO must support enforced MFA via our IdP and SCIM provisioning for deprovisioning access.
15:55 Speaker 3 (Riley): supported, we'll provide SCIM mappings and SAML metadata. deprovisioning flows tested during pilot
16:20 Speaker 1 (Jordan): recap next steps: send security pack (SOC2/ISO/pen test), benchmark plan, cost worksheet, schedule PrivateLink checklist, and set benchmark dates. can we lock a date for the smoke run now?
16:40 Speaker 2 (Laura): aim for week of 7/20 for smoke, fine to confirm after you send the plan
16:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): great. any final questions?
17:05 Speaker 2 (Laura): none from me, thanks everyone
17:15 Speaker 3 (Riley): thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff
17:30 Meeting closed
